en: strongly; richly (of a smell or mood)

examples.ko: 가을 숲에서 낙엽 냄새가 물씬 났어요.
examples.en: The smell of fallen leaves rose strongly in the autumn forest.

examples.ko: 이 식당에 들어서면 옛날 분위기가 물씬 풍겨요.
examples.en: When you walk into this restaurant, an old-time atmosphere comes through strongly.
The smell of doenjang stew is wafting up strongly from the kitchen.
When the rain stopped, the smell of earth spread thickly.

examples.ko: 이 사진에서는 어린 시절의 향수가 물씬 느껴져요.
examples.en: You can strongly feel nostalgia for childhood in this photo.

examples.ko: 이곳은 시골 정취가 물씬 풍기는 마을이에요.
examples.en: This is a village that gives off a strong country charm.

explain: 냄새, 분위기, 느낌이 확 짙게 느껴질 때 써요. '풍기다, 나다, 느껴지다'와 자주 같이 나오고, 단순히 정도만 높이는 '아주'와는 쓰임이 달라요.
explain_en: Use it when a smell, mood or feeling comes across thick and strong. It often pairs with '풍기다', '나다' and '느껴지다', and it is not a plain intensifier like '아주'.

examples.ko: 해충 박멸을 위해 집 전체를 소독했어요.
examples.en: We disinfected the whole house to wipe out the pests.

examples.ko: 바퀴벌레 박멸은 한 번으로 끝나지 않아요.
examples.en: Getting rid of cockroaches for good doesn't end with one treatment.

examples.ko: 요즘 같은 여름에 모기 박멸이 정말 가능할까요?
examples.en: Is it really possible to wipe out mosquitoes in a summer like this?

examples.ko: 이 업체는 개미 박멸을 전문으로 해요.
examples.en: This company specializes in exterminating ants.
The government announced a plan to eradicate the disease.

examples.ko: 박멸이 어려운 이유는 알이 숨어 있기 때문이에요.
examples.en: The reason it's hard to wipe them out is that the eggs are hidden.

explain: '퇴치'가 쫓아내거나 물리치는 느낌이라면 '박멸'은 뿌리째 완전히 없앤다는 느낌이 더 강해요. 보통 '해충 박멸', '질병 박멸'처럼 써요.
explain_en: '퇴치' feels like driving something off or beating it, while '박멸' stresses wiping it out completely. It usually appears in phrases like '해충 박멸' and '질병 박멸'.

examples.ko: 집에 있는 바퀴벌레를 완전히 박멸하고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to completely wipe out the cockroaches in my house.
This product kills off mold.

examples.ko: 전문 업체가 우리 집 개미를 박멸했어요.
examples.en: A professional company exterminated the ants in our house.
To wipe out pests, you have to get rid of the eggs too.
It isn't easy to eradicate this disease.

examples.ko: 텃밭의 잡초를 박멸하는 방법 좀 알려 주세요.
examples.en: Please tell me how to wipe out the weeds in my garden plot.

explain: '없애다'보다 딱딱하고, 하나도 안 남기고 없앤다는 느낌이 강해요. 일상 대화에서는 '잡다, 없애다'가 더 자연스럽고, '박멸하다'는 광고나 뉴스에서 많이 보여요.
explain_en: It is stiffer than '없애다' and suggests leaving nothing behind. In daily talk '잡다' or '없애다' sounds more natural, while '박멸하다' shows up in ads and news.

examples.ko: 새 휴대폰이라고 해도 별반 다르지 않아요.
examples.en: Even though it's a new phone, it's not all that different.
I don't have much to do today.

examples.ko: 그 일에 대해 별반 관심이 없어요.
examples.en: I'm not particularly interested in that matter.

examples.ko: 약을 먹어도 별반 차이를 못 느끼겠어요.
examples.en: Even after taking the medicine, I don't notice much difference.

examples.ko: 이 식당은 소문과 달리 맛이 별반 특별하지 않아요.
examples.en: Unlike the rumors, the food at this restaurant isn't particularly special.

examples.ko: 병원에 갔는데 별반 문제는 없다고 했어요.
examples.en: I went to the hospital and they said there was no particular problem.

explain: 뒤에 '없다, 아니다, 않다' 같은 부정 표현이 와야 해요. '별로'와 뜻이 비슷하지만 '별반'은 조금 딱딱해서 글이나 격식 있는 말에서 더 어울려요.
explain_en: It needs a negative ending such as '없다', '아니다' or '않다'. It is close to '별로' but a bit stiffer, so it fits writing and formal speech better.

examples.en: I supported Grandma at her side so she wouldn't fall.

examples.ko: 다리를 다친 친구를 부축해서 병원에 갔어요.
examples.en: I supported my friend, who hurt his leg, and we went to the hospital.
Please help the elderly person on the stairs.
He walked while supporting his stumbling father.
I'll support you, so please get up slowly.

examples.ko: 아픈 동생을 부축하는 모습이 보기 좋았어요.
examples.en: It was nice to see him supporting his sick younger sibling.

explain: 몸이 불편한 사람의 팔이나 몸을 잡고 걷거나 일어나게 도울 때 써서, 그냥 '돕다'보다 동작이 구체적이에요. 어르신께는 '부축해 드리다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is used when you hold someone's arm or body so they can walk or stand, which makes it more physical than plain '돕다'. For an elder, say '부축해 드리다'.

examples.en: The police found the criminal gang's hideout.
I heard that building was a den of thieves.

examples.ko: 영화 속 악당은 산속 소굴에 숨어 있었어요.
examples.en: The villain in the movie was hiding in a lair in the mountains.

examples.ko: 우리 방은 완전히 쓰레기 소굴이 됐어요.
examples.en: Our room has turned into a complete pigsty.

examples.ko: 아이들이 놀고 나면 거실이 장난감 소굴처럼 변해요.
examples.en: After the kids play, the living room turns into a toy den.

examples.ko: 친구 집에 갔더니 게임 소굴로 변해 있었어요.
examples.en: When I went to my friend's house, it had turned into a gaming den.

explain: 나쁜 사람이나 범죄 무리가 모여 사는 본거지를 말하고, 비유로 지저분하거나 어수선한 곳에도 써요. '아지트'는 친구들끼리의 비밀 장소처럼 좋은 느낌으로도 쓰지만 '소굴'은 늘 부정적이에요.
explain_en: It means the base where bad people or criminals gather, and figuratively a filthy or chaotic place. '아지트' can feel friendly, like a secret spot for friends, but '소굴' is always negative.

examples.en: A search party is looking for the missing hiker.
The search party combed the mountain all night.
They put together a search party of firefighters and soldiers.

examples.ko: 수색대에 지원한 사람이 백 명이 넘어요.
examples.en: More than a hundred people volunteered for the search party.
The rescue dogs also moved together with the search party.
Thanks to the search party's efforts, we found the child.

explain: 실종이나 조난 뉴스에서 자주 나오는 말이에요. '구조대'는 사람을 구하는 팀이고, '수색대'는 먼저 찾아다니는 팀이라는 점이 달라요.
explain_en: It often appears in news about missing or stranded people. A '구조대' is a team that rescues people, while a '수색대' is the team that goes out to find them first.

examples.ko: 동생은 자는 시늉하면서 제 말을 다 들었어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling pretended to sleep while listening to everything I said.

examples.ko: 아이가 의사처럼 청진기를 대는 시늉을 해요.
examples.en: The child pretends to put a stethoscope on like a doctor.

examples.ko: 그는 바쁜 시늉을 했지만 사실 할 일이 없었어요.
examples.en: He pretended to be busy, but he actually had nothing to do.

examples.ko: 친구가 우는 시늉을 하며 저를 웃겼어요.
examples.en: My friend made me laugh by pretending to cry.

examples.ko: 모르는 시늉하지 말고 솔직하게 말해 주세요.
examples.en: Don't pretend you don't know, and tell me honestly.
Don't just go through the motions of studying, focus.

explain: '~는 시늉을 하다'로 띄어 쓰는 경우가 훨씬 흔해요. 진짜는 아닌데 그런 모습이나 동작을 겉으로 흉내 낸다는 느낌이라서, '척하다'와 비슷하게 쓸 수 있어요.
explain_en: It is much more common to say '~는 시늉을 하다' as separate words. It means imitating the look or motion of something without it being real, so it can often be used much like '척하다'.

examples.en: My grandfather was admitted to the hospital with heart failure.

examples.ko: 심부전 환자는 짠 음식을 줄여야 해요.
examples.en: People with heart failure need to cut down on salty food.

examples.ko: 심부전 증상이 나타나서 약을 먹기 시작했어요.
examples.en: Symptoms of heart failure appeared, so he started taking medication.
My mother has had heart failure for a long time.

examples.ko: 심부전이 심해지면 숨이 차고 다리가 부어요.
examples.en: When heart failure gets worse, you get short of breath and your legs swell.

examples.ko: 의사가 심부전 검사를 받아 보라고 했어요.
examples.en: The doctor told me to get tested for heart failure.

explain: '심장병'은 심장 관련 병을 넓게 부르는 말이고, 심부전은 그중 심장이 제 힘을 못 내는 상태를 가리키는 병명이에요. 병원이나 뉴스에서 나오고, 어른께는 '앓고 계시다'라고 높여요.
explain_en: '심장병' is a broad word for heart diseases, while '심부전' is a specific diagnosis where the heart can't work as strongly as it should. It appears at hospitals and in the news, and for an elder you say '앓고 계시다'.

examples.en: Try estimating the length by eye.

examples.ko: 사람이 몇 명쯤 올지 어림하기 어려워요.
examples.en: It's hard to guess roughly how many people will come.

examples.ko: 대충 어림해도 오천 원은 넘을 거예요.
examples.en: Even a rough estimate says it will be over five thousand won.
I judged the weight of the bag by hand and told them.
I estimated the time and set out, and I wasn't late.
The value I estimated was almost the same as the real one.

explain: 정확히 재지 않고 대충 짐작해서 헤아린다는 뜻이에요. 일상에서는 '어림잡다'나 '어림짐작'이 더 자주 들리고, '어림없다'와는 뜻이 달라요.

phrases.example: 한 시간 안에 이 많은 일을 끝내겠다고요? 어림도 없어요.
phrases.en: You think you can finish all this in an hour? No way.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가능성이 전혀 없다고 강하게 말할 때 써요. 상대의 기대나 요구를 단호하게 거절하는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say something is completely out of the question. It firmly rejects someone's hope or demand.

explain_en: It means roughly gauging something without measuring it exactly. In daily talk '어림잡다' and '어림짐작' are heard more often, and '어림없다' has a different meaning.

en: outside of a building; outside of a house

examples.ko: 이번 음악회는 비가 안 오면 옥외에서 열려요.
examples.en: This concert will be held outdoors if it doesn't rain.

examples.ko: 옥외 광고판이 너무 밝아서 눈이 부셔요.
examples.en: The outdoor billboard is so bright that it dazzles my eyes.

examples.ko: 옥외 주차장이라서 비가 오면 차가 젖어요.
examples.en: It's an outdoor parking lot, so the car gets wet when it rains.
For outdoor performances, the weather is really important.

examples.ko: 옥외에 설치된 안내판이 잘 보이지 않아요.
examples.en: The sign installed outside is hard to see.

examples.ko: 우리 회사는 옥외 운동 시설도 갖추고 있어요.
examples.en: Our company also has outdoor exercise facilities.

explain: 건물 밖을 뜻하고 반의어는 '옥내'예요. 광고, 안내문, 시설 설명 같은 딱딱한 글에 많고, 일상 대화에서는 '밖, 야외'라고 해요.
explain_en: It means outside a building, and its opposite is '옥내'. It appears in stiff writing such as ads, notices and facility descriptions, while in daily talk people say '밖' or '야외'.

examples.en: Our team won a complete victory in the final.
Today's game was a total win from start to finish.
We expected an easy win, but it was unexpectedly close.
We started the tournament with a clean win, so the mood is good.

examples.ko: 상대가 약해서 완승이 쉬울 줄 알았어요.
examples.en: I thought a total win would be easy because the opponent was weak.
A complete win in the very first game of the season, that's amazing.

explain: '완승을 거두다'로 자주 쓰고 반의어는 '완패'예요. 스포츠뿐 아니라 선거에서도 쓰며, '압승'은 큰 차이로 이긴다는 느낌이 더 강해요.
explain_en: It commonly appears as '완승을 거두다', and its opposite is '완패'. It is used in elections as well as sports, and '압승' puts more stress on winning by a big margin.

examples.en: People say there is no easy road to studying.
There is no royal road that leads to success.
The sure way to get good at English is steady practice.
Wouldn't it be nice if dieting had an easy way?

examples.ko: 선생님은 쉬운 왕도를 찾지 말라고 하셨어요.
examples.en: The teacher told us not to look for an easy shortcut.

examples.ko: 건강에도 왕도는 없고 좋은 습관이 중요해요.
examples.en: Health has no easy road either, and good habits matter.

explain: 거의 '왕도가 없다'의 꼴로 나와서, 쉽고 확실한 방법은 없다는 뜻을 전해요. '지름길'은 빨리 가는 길이라는 느낌이 강하고, '왕도'는 쉽고 정석적인 방법이라는 느낌이에요.

phrases.example: 공부에는 왕도가 없어요. 매일 조금씩 하는 게 최고예요.
phrases.en: There's no royal road to studying. Doing a little every day is best.
phrases.nuance_ko: 쉽고 빠른 길은 없고 꾸준히 노력해야 한다는 뜻으로 써요. 공부, 운동, 성공 같은 이야기에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: It says there is no easy or quick path and that steady effort is needed. It often comes up when talking about study, exercise or success.
phrases.en_equiv: there is no royal road to ~

explain_en: It almost always appears as '왕도가 없다', meaning there is no easy, sure method. '지름길' stresses a quicker way, while '왕도' suggests an easy, standard route.

examples.en: This city is a key transportation hub.
Since long ago, that island has been a strategic military point.
Because it has a port, it grew into a key trading center.
A new station is going to be built at the key location.

examples.ko: 여기는 길이 만나는 요충지라서 늘 붐벼요.
examples.en: This is a crossroads where roads meet, so it's always crowded.

examples.ko: 경쟁 회사들이 이 요충지를 차지하려고 해요.
examples.en: Rival companies are trying to take this key location.

explain: '교통의 요충지', '군사 요충지'처럼 길이 모이거나 지켜야 하는 중요한 곳에 써요. '중심지'는 사람과 활동이 모인 곳이고, '요충지'는 위치상 꼭 필요한 곳이라는 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: It is used for a place where routes meet or that must be protected, as in '교통의 요충지' and '군사 요충지'. '중심지' is where people and activity gather, while '요충지' is a place that matters because of its position.

examples.en: I read Aesop's fables and wrote a book report.
This story is a fable that criticizes greed.
The animals in fables talk like people.
The teacher told us to find the lesson in the fable.

examples.ko: 이 만화는 현대 사회를 풍자한 우화로 평가돼요.
examples.en: This comic is regarded as a fable that satirizes modern society.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 읽은 우화가 아직도 기억나요.
examples.en: I still remember a fable I read as a child.

explain: '동화'는 어린이를 위한 이야기 전체를 말하고, '우화'는 동물이나 사물에 빗대어 교훈이나 풍자를 전하는 이야기예요. '이솝 우화'가 가장 잘 알려진 예예요.
explain_en: '동화' covers children's stories in general, while '우화' is a story that uses animals or objects to deliver a lesson or satire. 'Aesop's fables' ('이솝 우화') is the best-known example.

examples.ko: 오늘은 왠지 안 좋은 일이 생길 것 같은 육감이 들어요.
examples.en: I have a gut feeling that something bad will happen today.

examples.ko: 그의 육감은 틀린 적이 거의 없어요.
examples.en: His hunches are almost never wrong.
The detective sensed who the criminal was by intuition.

examples.ko: 육감을 믿고 다른 길로 갔더니 안 막혔어요.
examples.en: I trusted my gut and took another road, and there was no traffic.
Even my intuition is wrong sometimes.
I decided by my gut feeling, and the result was good.

explain: 눈, 귀 같은 오감으로 설명할 수 없는 직감을 가리켜요. 일상에서는 '촉'이라는 말도 쓰고, '육감적'은 몸매가 관능적이라는 다른 뜻이니 주의하세요.
explain_en: It refers to a hunch that the five senses can't explain. In daily talk people also say '촉', and be careful because '육감적' has a different meaning, describing a sensual body.

examples.en: Our department head is a person who is blessed with good people around him.

examples.ko: 저는 인덕 하나는 타고난 것 같아요.
examples.en: I think I was born with luck when it comes to people.

examples.ko: 그가 빨리 승진한 건 인덕 덕분이에요.
examples.en: He got promoted quickly thanks to the people who helped him.
Having people on your side doesn't happen overnight.
That person has both good people around them and real skill.

examples.ko: 인덕을 쌓으려면 평소에 남에게 잘해야 해요.
examples.en: To build up goodwill from others, you have to treat people well in daily life.

explain: 주변에서 사람들이 도와주고 따르는 복을 말하고, 일상에서는 '인복'이라고도 해요. '인덕이 있다/많다/없다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It describes the good fortune of having people around who help and support you, and in daily talk it is also called '인복'. It is used as '인덕이 있다/많다/없다'.

examples.en: That person is the right fit for the team leader position.
A meticulous person is just right for this job.

examples.ko: 적격 심사를 통과해야 계약할 수 있어요.
examples.en: You have to pass the eligibility review to sign the contract.

examples.ko: 심사 결과 두 팀이 적격으로 판정됐어요.
examples.en: After the review, two teams were judged eligible.
What kind of person would be right for this role?

examples.ko: 그는 선생님으로서 적격은 아닌 것 같아요.
examples.en: I don't think he is suited to be a teacher.

explain: 주로 '~에 적격이다'로 쓰고, 자격이나 조건에 딱 맞는다는 판단이 담겨 있어요. 반의어는 '부적격'이에요.
explain_en: It is mostly used as '~에 적격이다' and carries a judgment that someone or something fits the qualifications or conditions exactly. Its opposite is '부적격'.

examples.en: The soldiers secretly entered enemy territory.
Going deep into enemy lines is dangerous.
The soldier who went to scout the enemy position came back.

examples.ko: 영화 속 주인공은 혼자 적진에 뛰어들었어요.
examples.en: The hero in the movie jumped into the enemy camp alone.
It took two days to get out of the enemy camp.
In soccer, the striker waits near the opponent's side.

explain: 전쟁뿐 아니라 게임이나 스포츠에서 상대편 진영을 가리킬 때도 써요. '적진에 뛰어들다'처럼 상대의 영역으로 들어간다는 뜻으로 비유하기도 해요.
explain_en: Besides war, it can mean the opposing side's area in games and sports. It is also used figuratively, as in '적진에 뛰어들다', for entering the other side's territory.

examples.en: The police finally caught the real culprit.
Evidence came out that the real culprit is someone else.
In the final episode, the real culprit was an unexpected person.

examples.ko: 처음에 잡힌 사람은 진범과 아무 관계가 없었어요.
examples.en: The person first caught had nothing to do with the real culprit.

examples.ko: 모두가 그를 진범으로 믿었지만 사실은 아니었어요.
examples.en: Everyone believed he was the real culprit, but he wasn't.

examples.ko: 누가 진범인지 끝까지 알 수 없었어요.
examples.en: We couldn't tell who the real culprit was until the end.

explain: 다른 사람이 억울하게 의심받을 때 '진짜 범인'을 가리키는 말이에요. '진범을 잡다/밝히다', '진범이 따로 있다'처럼 자주 써요.
explain_en: It points to the true criminal, especially when someone else has been wrongly suspected. It is often used as '진범을 잡다/밝히다' and '진범이 따로 있다'.

examples.en: The child is smiling innocently.
Everyone smiled at the child's innocent expression.
That child is cute because of the innocent way he talks.
He is really innocent for his age.
The way he played with the puppy was truly innocent.

examples.ko: 아이들은 천진스럽지만 때로는 너무 솔직해서 놀라요.
examples.en: Kids are innocent, but sometimes so frank that I'm startled.

explain: 꾸밈없이 순수하고 어린아이 같은 모습에 써요. 'ㅂ 불규칙'이라 '천진스러워요'가 되고, '천진난만하다'와 함께 자주 들려요.
explain_en: It describes a natural, pure, childlike manner. It is a ㅂ-irregular adjective, so it becomes '천진스러워요', and it is often heard alongside '천진난만하다'.

examples.en: The general was appointed commander-in-chief of the whole army.
The supreme commander visited the front line in person.

examples.ko: 역사 영화에서 총사령관은 늘 지도를 보고 있어요.
examples.en: In historical movies, the commander-in-chief is always looking at a map.
In this game, I'm the supreme commander.
All the units moved on the commander-in-chief's order.

examples.ko: 새 총사령관을 누구로 뽑을지 논의 중이에요.
examples.en: They are discussing who to choose as the new commander-in-chief.

explain: 군 전체를 이끄는 가장 높은 지휘관을 말해요. '사령관'은 한 부대의 지휘관도 되지만 '총사령관'은 전체를 맡는다는 점이 달라요.
explain_en: It refers to the top commander who leads the entire military. A '사령관' can command a single unit, while a '총사령관' is in charge of everything.

examples.en: A scandal about the celebrity came out in the news.

examples.ko: 그 정치인은 추문 때문에 자리에서 물러났어요.
examples.en: That politician stepped down because of a scandal.
The company was caught up in a scandal, and its stock price fell.
I heard they lied to cover up the scandal.
Rumors and scandals spread fast.
The singer whose image suffered from a scandal made a comeback.

explain: 도덕적으로 좋지 않은 일이 소문이나 기사로 알려진 것을 말해요. 일상 대화에서는 '스캔들'이라고 많이 하고, '추문'은 기사나 글에서 더 자주 보여요.
explain_en: It means a morally embarrassing matter that has become known through rumor or news. In everyday talk people often say '스캔들', while '추문' shows up more in articles and writing.

examples.en: My older brother took over our father's family business.
Our family business has been farming for generations.

examples.ko: 이 가게는 삼대째 가업으로 이어지고 있어요.
examples.en: This shop has been passed down as a family business for three generations.
A family business is often passed on to one's children.
My father devoted his whole life to the family business.

examples.ko: 가업도 시대에 맞게 바뀌어야 한다고 생각해요.
examples.en: I think even a family business has to change with the times.

explain: 대대로 집안에서 이어 오는 일을 말하고, '가업을 잇다/물려받다/물려주다'처럼 써요. 그냥 '가게'와 달리 대를 이어 간다는 뜻이 들어 있어요.
explain_en: It means the work a family carries on over generations, used as '가업을 잇다/물려받다/물려주다'. Unlike a plain '가게', it carries the idea of handing it down.

examples.ko: 새 규칙은 한 달간 계도 기간을 거쳐요.
examples.en: The new rule goes through a one-month grace period for guidance.

examples.ko: 경찰은 처벌보다 계도에 중점을 두고 있어요.
examples.en: The police are focusing on guidance rather than punishment.

examples.ko: 시민 의식 계도를 위한 캠페인이 열려요.
examples.en: A campaign to raise citizens' awareness will be held.

examples.ko: 벌금을 내기 전에 계도부터 해야 한다고 해요.
examples.en: They say guidance should come before fines.
This banner was put up for the purpose of educating the public.
For the sake of guidance, we only gave a warning this time.

explain: '처벌'과 맞서는 말로 쓰여요. 단속 뉴스에서 '계도 기간'에는 벌금 대신 안내와 경고만 하고, 그 뒤에 본격적으로 단속해요. '계도 위주', '계도 차원'처럼 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is the counterpart of '처벌' (punishment). In enforcement news, during a '계도 기간' people are only informed and warned instead of fined, and strict enforcement starts afterward. It often appears as '계도 위주' and '계도 차원'.

examples.en: A campaign to educate citizens was held.
The police guided the people who were breaking the rules.

examples.ko: 처벌보다 먼저 계도해야 한다는 목소리가 커요.
examples.en: More people are saying we should educate before punishing.
The school tries to guide students in the right direction.
We guided the staff and prevented the same mistake.

examples.ko: 계도하기보다 스스로 깨닫게 하는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: It's better to let them realize it themselves than to guide them from above.

explain: 윗사람이나 기관이 대중을 가르쳐 바르게 이끈다는 느낌이라서 개인끼리 이야기할 때는 거의 안 써요. 일상에서는 '가르치다, 타이르다'가 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: It feels like an authority or institution teaching and steering the public, so it is rarely used between individuals. In daily talk '가르치다' or '타이르다' sounds more natural.

examples.ko: 모든 논의는 결국 돈 문제로 귀결돼요.
examples.en: Every discussion ends up boiling down to money.
The debate ended up at the same conclusion.

examples.ko: 이 문제는 결국 교육의 질로 귀결되는 것 같아요.
examples.en: It seems this issue comes down to the quality of education.
I think all worries come down to health.
The negotiation ended without reaching an agreement.
I didn't know the story would end up like this.

explain: '~로 귀결되다'의 꼴로 쓰고, 이야기나 과정이 마지막에 하나의 결론으로 모인다는 뜻이에요. 토론이나 글에서 자주 나오고, 말할 때는 '결국 ~로 끝나다'라고 해도 돼요.
explain_en: It is used as '~로 귀결되다', meaning a discussion or process finally converges on one conclusion. It is common in debates and writing, and in speech you can say '결국 ~로 끝나다' instead.

examples.en: The policy difference between the two candidates is stark.

examples.ko: 이번 시험 결과는 노력의 차이를 극명하게 보여 줬어요.
examples.en: The results of this exam clearly showed the difference in effort.

examples.ko: 극명한 대비가 사진을 더 인상적으로 만들어요.
examples.en: The sharp contrast makes the photo more striking.

examples.ko: 결과 발표 후 두 팀의 표정이 극명하게 갈렸어요.
examples.en: After the results were announced, the two teams' expressions were starkly different.
The difference isn't clear-cut, so it's hard to tell them apart.

examples.ko: 서울과 시골의 생활 방식 차이가 극명해서 놀랐어요.
examples.en: I was surprised by how stark the difference in lifestyle between Seoul and the countryside is.

explain: 주로 '극명한 차이', '극명한 대비'처럼 둘이 확연히 갈리는 것에 어울려요. 그냥 '분명하다'보다 차이가 선명하게 드러난다는 느낌이 강해요.
explain_en: It fits best with things that split sharply, as in '극명한 차이' and '극명한 대비'. Compared with plain '분명하다', it stresses that the difference stands out vividly.
